title: Lead Time Uncertainty and Hydrogen Infrastructure Investment: A System Dynamics Analysis of Capacity Expansion, Demand Foresight, and Market Effects
content:
This study examines how uncertainty in infrastructure construction lead times affects the cost, performance, and resilience of Sweden’s hydrogen transition using system dynamics modeling. A comprehensive uncertainty analysis was performed, combining five investment planning scenarios with 64 lead time combinations for hydrogen production facilities, electricity grid reinforcement, and hydrogen pipeline infrastructure. To assess the influence of investment behavior, the study compared three capacity expansion strategies: Baseline, Reactive, and Proactive. Two additional scenarios examined the effects of short and long demand foresight horizons on investment timing and system performance. 

Reactive investment strategies achieve higher capacity utilization and lower consumer costs when infrastructure lead time is shorter. However, they become highly vulnerable to supply shortages and price spikes under delayed deployment conditions. In contrast, proactive capacity expansion strategies improve system resilience, maintain higher demand satisfaction, and substantially reduce the cost impact of longer infrastructure delays. The analysis shows that extending the demand foresight horizon is more effective than increasing capacity buffers, highlighting the value of improved market information and long-term planning. From a policy perspective, the findings suggest that reducing construction lead times, improving cross-infrastructure coordination, and lowering investment risk can deliver greater system-wide benefits than technology cost reductions alone.
